content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed to quantify the subjectivity of image aesthetics using uncertainty mass from the beta distribution. The author also designed a simultaneous learning framework to predict the rating distribution and subjectivity simultaneously. Experiments about subjectivity regression and various aesthetic assessment tasks are conducted on a commonly used dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:  
1. This paper introduced the uncertainty metric of binomial opinion-beta mapping into image aesthetic assessment.
2. This paper is easy to understand.

Weakness:  
1. The author claimed "if the rating scale is normalized between 0 and 1, the rating can be considered as a binomial opinion indicating the subjective belief about aesthetic pleasingness of the image", but the meanings of a rating scale and the subjective belief seem different. Such as a rating scale of 6 means the aesthetic is slightly above average, while a subjective belief of 0.6 indicates that the rating has a 60% confidence level. Thus, the conversion between rating and subjectivity doesn't seem reasonable.
2. What is the intention of the author to predict the subjectivity of image aesthetics? From the experiment, the subjectivity prediction does not help other common image aesthetic assessment tasks. The author said that subjectivity predicting can be used for image recommendation. However, similar recommendations can be made by calculating the variance of rating prediction instead of predicting subjectivity.
3. Compared with other metrics (STD, MAD, DUD, MED), what are the advantages of AesU? The author said that other metrics are not well interpretable, but there is no intuitive comparison or case study. From Table 1, the performances of predicting the AesU and other metrics are not much different.
4. There is no well theoretical support for aesthetic rating distribution obeying beta distribution.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is easy to understand, but it lacks novelty. The theoretical basis and experimental analysis do not well support the proposed idea.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a unified probabilistic framework for modeling and quantifying the
subjectivity of image aesthetics based on the subjective logic, in which the rating distribution of an image is modeled as a beta distribution and the probability of being uncertain obtained from the distribution defines a subjectivity metric. Moreover, authors propose to train a deep neural networks for the prediction of the subjectivity metrics and present experiments applying the proposed model to the aesthetics-based image recommendation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
strengths:
1)	Authors propose a unified probabilistic framework to address both image aesthetic assessment task and aesthetic subjectivity regression task.
2)	Authors propose to model and quantify the subjectivity in aesthetic assessment based on the transferred aesthetic rating distribution (beta distribution). They also propose an intuitive metric of subjectivity.
3)	The experiments show that the proposed model improves the performance of subjectivity regression compared to the conventional aesthetic assessment approaches.
weaknesses:
1)	The aesthetic rating distribution itself can give subjectivity related information and the superiority of the proposed subjectivity metric over common used metrics is not convincing.
2)	Recent methods of image aesthetic assessment generally can perform binary classification, mean score regression, and rating distribution prediction simultaneously, the novelty for this part is limited.
3)	The performance improvement of the proposed approach on aesthetic assessment task is marginal.
4)	All experiments are tested only on AVA dataset, which is not sufficient for the evaluation and genera of the method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
clarity: Good. The paper is well organized but the presentation has minor details that could be improved.
quality: Poor. The paper has major technical flaws, and the experimental evaluation is flawed and fails to adequately support the main claims.
novelty: Poor. The main ideas of the paper have limited novelty.
reproducibility: Good. Sufficient details (e.g., experimental settings and implement details) are described such that an expert should be able to reproduce the main results.
content.summary_of_the_review: As discussed above, both the novelty and performance improvement of this paper are marginal. Moreover, the authors only present the results on single dataset and compare with only one baselines. Therefore, I am not convinced that this paper is sufficient for acceptance.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors proposed a unified probabilistic framework for modeling image aesthetics, particularly considering proper quantification of the subjectivity. In particular, the framework allows to model the rating distribution as a beta distribution and to obtain the probabilities of being definitely pleasing, being definitely unpleasing, and being uncertain simultaneously. The authors also present an application scenario where the framework is beneficial for aesthetics-based image recommendation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

The paper works on an interesting and practical problem. The whole paper reads smoothly. The presentation and illustration of this paper is clear. 

Weakness:

I’m a bit unsure about the evaluation of the results.  The authors used PLCC, SROCC and MAE to measure the subjectivity regression. However, I’m wondering if these metrics enough for subjectivity evaluation? There are cases where the regression results are the same, but the subjectivity statuses are different. 

The authors defined a new metric quantifying the level of subjectivity, called aesthetic subjectivity (AesU) and claimed that it has several advantages compared to the existing
metrics. It would be better if the authors could show and discuss these advantages during the experiments. 

Can the authors compare the time cost for proposed model (simultaneous learning) and conventional approach? 

Minor: 
1) Who are the raters in the evaluation of the recommendation application scenarios?
2) It is better to explain the definitions of PLCC, SROCC when they first appear in Table 1 in page 6. As their definitions are only shown in page 7.

content.summary_of_the_review: The paper works on an interesting problem. However, as mentioned above in the weakness part, I feel some more discussions about the evaluation and motivation are needed.

content.title: Unified Probabilistic Modeling of Image Aesthetic Rating Distributions towards Measuring Subjectivity
content.abstract: Assessing image aesthetics is a challenging computer vision task. One reason is that aesthetic preference is highly subjective and may vary significantly among people for certain images. Thus, it is important to properly model and quantify such subjectivity, but there has not been much effort to resolve this issue. In this paper, we propose a novel unified probabilistic framework that can model and quantify subjective aesthetic preference based on the subjective logic. In this framework, the distribution of aesthetic ratings is modeled as a beta distribution, from which the probabilities of being definitely pleasing, being definitely unpleasing, and being uncertain can be obtained. We use the probability of being uncertain to define an intuitive metric of subjectivity. Furthermore, we present a method to learn deep neural networks for prediction of image aesthetics, which is shown to be effective in improving the performance of subjectivity prediction via experiments. We also present an application scenario where the framework is beneficial for aesthetics-based image recommendation.
